newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Chinese official blames Taiwan for souring ties.
newsitem.headline: Chinese official blames Taiwan for souring ties.

text.p: A visiting Chinese official on Tuesday blamed Taiwan for more than two years of non-dialogue and sour relations across the Taiwan Strait.

"Everybody knows why (cross-strait) talks were suspended. We are not the one to blame," Liu Gangqi, deputy secretary-general of China's semi-official Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Strait, told reporters.

Beijing, which regards Taiwan as a renegade province, indefinitely suspended quasi-official talks with Taipei after Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui made a private, but high-profile, visit to the United States in 1995.
Lee's trip also prompted China to stage rounds of intimidating war games near Taiwan to counter what it perceived as a growing independence movement on the island.
Liu, the highest-level mainland representative to visit Taiwan since Taipei-Beijing ties froze in 1995, said the resumption of talks would depend on "certain conditions and a right atmosphere."
"Everybody knows what are these (conditions and atmosphere)," Liu said.
Beijing has said that only when Taiwan, which split from the mainland after the Chinese civil war ended in 1949, complies with the "one-China" principle would it allow a resumption of talks.

Beijing considers Taiwan a part of Chinese territory that must be brought under the mainland's eventual rule. Taipei says it wants to unite with mainland China, but maintains it is currently a sovereign government independent of Beijing's control.
The mainland association's Taiwan counterpart, the Straits Exchange Foundation, said a resumption of talks did not depend on "atmosphere."
"It is sincerity that counts," said Chiao Jen-ho, the foundation's vice chairman.
Local news media in Taiwan said Liu's visit was a sign of slowly warming relations between the long-time rivals.

But Liu, who arrived here on Monday with some 30 Chinese scholars to attend a two-day seminar on the modernisation of China, said he came to Taiwan not to discuss the resumption of talks but "just to attend the seminar."
